title: Assess cloud, container, API, and serverless security paths: concept decisions 1
teachingQuestion: Who owns each control at this cloud service boundary, and what could misuse it?
focalInsight: Service model changes operations; tenant identity, configuration, data, integration, and evidence remain accountable.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Cloud Security
nodes.definition: Protection of cloud data, identity, configuration, integration, operations, and contracts.
nodes.detail: Protection of cloud data, identity, configuration, integration, operations, and contracts.
nodes.decision: Evaluate the actual tenant configuration and service layer, not the cloud label.
nodes.failureExample: A public object store exposes data despite provider infrastructure security.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Cloud security includes customer-controlled settings and evidence.

nodes.label: Shared Responsibility
nodes.definition: Explicit division of who operates and assures each cloud control layer.
nodes.detail: Explicit division of who operates and assures each cloud control layer.
nodes.decision: Assign provider and customer actions for identity, data, network, logs, backups, and incidents.
nodes.failureExample: Neither party monitors a customer-controlled access rule.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: An unassigned responsibility is an unmanaged risk.

nodes.label: Saas
nodes.definition: Provider application consumed by the customer, with customer configuration and data-use duties.
nodes.detail: Provider application consumed by the customer, with customer configuration and data-use duties.
nodes.decision: Focus on tenant access, sharing, data handling, integration, and contractual evidence.
nodes.failureExample: A SaaS collaboration space retains an open default sharing policy.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: SaaS reduces infrastructure operation, not tenant governance.

nodes.label: Iaas
nodes.definition: Provider processing, storage, and networking on which the customer manages more of the stack.
nodes.detail: Provider processing, storage, and networking on which the customer manages more of the stack.
nodes.decision: Focus on guest OS, workload, virtual network, identities, and configuration.
nodes.failureExample: An IaaS guest remains unpatched because the customer assumes the provider does it.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: IaaS leaves substantial customer administration responsibility.

nodes.label: Paas
nodes.decision: Focus on application code, identities, data, configurations, integrations, and platform limits.
nodes.failureExample: An application exposes credentials in a PaaS configuration variable.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: PaaS changes the boundary; it does not remove application responsibility.

nodes.label: Microservices
nodes.definition: Many collaborating services with separate deployment and communication boundaries.
nodes.detail: Many collaborating services with separate deployment and communication boundaries.
nodes.decision: Give each service a workload identity and authorize each call.
nodes.failureExample: A mesh routes calls but a service accepts an unauthenticated internal request.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Network routing is not service authorization.

nodes.label: API Security
nodes.definition: Server-side enforcement of authenticated, authorized, validated API actions.
nodes.detail: Server-side enforcement of authenticated, authorized, validated API actions.
nodes.decision: Check caller, object, action, input, rate, and audit context at each endpoint.
nodes.failureExample: A token holder accesses another tenant’s object by changing an API parameter.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Authorize the specific object and action on the server.

nodes.label: Containerization
nodes.definition: Deployment of packaged workload images under a runtime and orchestration context.
nodes.detail: Deployment of packaged workload images under a runtime and orchestration context.
nodes.decision: Control image provenance, registry access, runtime privilege, secrets, and network policy.
nodes.failureExample: A stale image with a vulnerable library is redeployed from an unprotected registry.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: The image and control plane are part of the security boundary.

nodes.label: Serverless
nodes.definition: Event-triggered managed execution with function-specific identities and dependencies.
nodes.detail: Event-triggered managed execution with function-specific identities and dependencies.
nodes.decision: Validate event origin and payload; bound permission, retries, and side effects.
nodes.failureExample: A replayed event causes a function to create the same privileged record repeatedly.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Use authorization and idempotence where repeated events matter.
